title: Reclaim cleanup target
description: One cleanable location (or delegated command): what the data is, where it lives, how risky it is to remove, and how Reclaim cleans it. One file per target under Catalogue/<category>/<id>.json. Full guide: docs/CATALOGUE.md.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema so editors validate and autocomplete the manifest. Always '../schema/target.schema.json'.

id.description: Stable, unique, kebab-case identifier. Must equal the file name without '.json'. Never rename a shipped id — user selection state is stored against it.

category.description: The tool family shown in the sidebar. Must equal the name of the directory this manifest lives in.

safety.description: How risky cleaning is. 'safe': regenerated automatically (build caches, logs). 'caution': restorable, but re-downloading or losing history costs something (models, session history, archives). 'destructive': removes things the user created (emulators, installed language versions). Rubric: docs/CATALOGUE.md.

paths.description: Path patterns resolved at scan time. '~' expands to the user's home; '*' globs within a single path component (e.g. '~/Library/Caches/Google/AndroidStudio*'). Patterns that do not exist on a machine are silently dropped, so listing several historical or candidate locations is fine. Each starts with '~/' or '/', no trailing slash. Omit only for command targets whose size cannot be measured.

strategy.description: How Reclaim cleans. 'removeContents': delete the children of each resolved directory but keep the directory — preferred for cache roots, tools expect them to exist. 'removePaths': delete each resolved path itself — only when removing the item is the point. 'command': delegate to an external executable (requires the 'command' object). 'manual': Reclaim measures but never deletes; the user is shown 'instructions' (required).

command.description: Companion for "strategy": "command" — the external tool that performs the cleanup safely on Reclaim's behalf.

executable.description: Absolute path to the executable. Never resolved via $PATH, so behavior is deterministic regardless of the user's shell.

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the executable, one array element each.

display.description: The human-readable command line shown in the UI, e.g. 'xcrun simctl delete unavailable'. Not localized — it is a literal command.

availabilityProbe.description: Optional path pattern that must resolve for the tool to count as installed (e.g. '~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator' for simctl — '/usr/bin/xcrun' exists on every Mac and proves nothing). Without a resolving probe the target scans as 'not installed' instead of 'unmeasurable'.

instructions.description: Companion for "strategy": "manual" — tells the user which tool to run instead, with the command in backticks, e.g. 'Run `docker system prune` in Terminal.'. Keep the backticked command identical in every language (test-enforced).

relatedApps.description: Bundle identifiers of apps that actively use this data. When one is running, the pre-clean confirmation warns the user (a soft warning, never a hard block). Set this for IDE and desktop-app caches.

name.description: Short display name shown as the row title, e.g. 'Derived data'.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what the data is and what happens after cleaning. Shown under the name.

note.description: Optional extra warning or tip surfaced in the row, e.g. 'Keep archives for versions that are live on the App Store.'

localizedText.description: Per-locale text. Every supported locale is required. Machine translation is acceptable for 'nb' — flag it in your PR so a native speaker reviews it.
